title: Vivid
tagline: A new instrument for live visuals.
meta_description: Vivid is a new instrument for live visuals: play sound and picture as one, rewire the signal path live, author your own operators with code and AI, and fork the whole thing. A macOS app for VJs, live performers, and creative technologists.
manifesto: Vivid is a new instrument for live visuals: play sound and picture as one, rewire the signal path live, author your own operators with code and AI, and fork the whole thing.
hero_lede: Play sound and picture as one signal path. Rewire the path between them live. Author your own operators with code and AI. Fork the whole thing. A project is a folder you own.
one_liner: A macOS app where a DAW-style Session View and a rewireable visual node graph are one project, so you play sound and picture together.

verbs.title: Play
verbs.body: Sound and picture are one signal path you perform in real time. A DAW-style Session View and a live visual graph share a single project: the notes you play are the picture you throw.

verbs.title: Rewire
verbs.body: The path between sound and picture is a live, rewireable node graph, not a fixed pipeline. Assemble it from typed operators and re-patch the signal flow while it runs.

verbs.title: Author
verbs.body: When a look doesn't exist yet, you write it - project-local WGSL shaders and compiled C++ operators, edited live. And every operation is exposed over MCP, so an AI agent authors, inspects and verifies whole projects alongside you.

verbs.title: Fork
verbs.body: A project is a folder you own end to end - the session, the graph, the mappings, and your custom operators, saved together. Take it, change it, run it anywhere. No lock-in, no cloud round-trip.

audiences.title: VJs & live visualists
audiences.body: Drive picture from your set in real time and rewire the look between songs - never wrestle a fixed pipeline mid-show.

audiences.title: Musicians & producers
audiences.body: Your Session View and the visuals are one project. Write the music and the picture it throws off together, and save both as one file.

audiences.title: Creative technologists & studios
audiences.body: Author operators in shaders and C++ with AI over MCP; fork a project folder straight into an installation or a client job.

audiences.title: Generative & new-media artists
audiences.body: Treat the graph as a sketchbook - patch, break, and reshape a living system that reacts to sound instead of a canned loop.

cta.title: Play it yourself.
cta.body: Download the signed macOS build and make your first audio-reactive project in a few minutes - or read the story behind the instrument.

supports.title: Session View
supports.body: A DAW-style timeline of tracks, clips, scenes, instruments, effects and a mixer - the musical half of the graph.

supports.title: Visual node graph
supports.body: A rewireable graph of visual operators (real geometry, shaders and compositing) that you build and fork like code.

supports.title: The mapping bridge
supports.body: A bidirectional bridge: musical and control signals drive visual parameters, and visual state can drive audio back.

supports.title: MCP-native control
supports.body: Every operation is exposed over MCP, so agents (and scripts) author, inspect and verify whole projects - not just nudge knobs.

tutorials.title: First MCP-native project
tutorials.build: A Surge XT track, a project-local shader, and audio mapped to visuals - saved as one portable, reloadable project.

tutorials.title: Live shader edit
tutorials.build: Discover a shader node's backing file, edit the WGSL and reload live, then deliberately break it and recover using Vivid's own diagnostics.

tutorials.title: Project C++ operator
tutorials.build: Scaffold a project-local C++ visual operator, compile it with clang++, and hot-swap it live after an edit.

guides.title: Make your first sound
guides.goal: Get a note out of Vivid - the shortest possible first win, no code, no visuals yet.

steps.do: Add a track and load the free Surge XT synth on it - Vivid finds it automatically once it's installed.
steps.see: A new track with Surge XT ready to play.

steps.do: Draw a short MIDI clip (a few notes) and press play.
steps.see: You hear Surge XT - Vivid is making sound.

guides.recap: That's the musical half of the instrument. Next, put something on screen.

guides.title: Put something on screen
guides.goal: Get a visual rendering in the output window - still no code.

steps.do: Open the visual node graph and add a visual operator - start with a built-in look or a shader.
steps.see: A shape or field appears in the graph.

steps.do: Add an Output node and connect your operator into it.
steps.see: Your visual fills the output window.

guides.recap: You have sound and picture. They're not talking to each other yet - that's the next, best part.

guides.title: Make it react to the sound
guides.goal: Map the sound onto the picture so the visual moves with the music - the aha.

steps.do: Open the mapping bridge and map an audio signal - a note's pitch, an envelope, a transient - onto a visual parameter like size or brightness.
steps.see: That parameter moves the instant the sound plays.

steps.do: Add a few more mappings - size, colour, glow - so several things react at once.
steps.see: The picture visibly moves with the music. This is the aha.

guides.recap: This is Vivid's whole idea: sound and picture are one signal path. The clip above is exactly this project, captured live.

guides.title: Perform it live
guides.goal: Arrange scenes and play sound and picture together in real time.

steps.do: Arrange your clips into scenes in the Session View.
steps.see: You can launch scenes and the visuals follow the change.

steps.do: Play the set - trigger scenes live and watch the look shift with the music.
steps.see: You're performing sound and picture as one instrument.

guides.recap: You can play Vivid. The clip above is a scene-driven performance made this way.

guides.title: Author your own - with code and AI
guides.goal: Graduate from playing the built-ins to writing your own operator - the deep end, and the point of Vivid.

steps.do: Open a shader node's backing WGSL file and edit it live - Vivid hot-reloads the change.
steps.see: Your edit shows up in the output immediately; break it and Vivid's diagnostics help you recover.

steps.do: Bring in an AI agent over MCP - ask it to author or tweak an operator, then inspect and verify the result together.
steps.see: You and the agent authored a new look, in code, over MCP.

guides.recap: You've gone from playing built-ins to authoring your own operators. From here, the tested code tutorials go deeper.

showcase.title: Your first project
showcase.blurb: The beginner project: a Surge XT track and a project-local shader whose rings pulse from four audio-to-visual mappings - the notes drive the picture, saved as a portable project.

showcase.title: Pulse
showcase.blurb: A techno scene driving a per-note geometry graph - hexagons for the bassline, wireframe octahedra for the lead, particle bursts on every drum hit.

showcase.title: Mirror
showcase.blurb: The bridge runs both ways: the music drives the picture, and the picture's feedback and blur drive a filter on the sound back.

showcase.title: Live shader edit
showcase.blurb: A woven interference field authored as a project-local WGSL shader - edited, broken and recovered live over MCP.

showcase.title: Neon
showcase.blurb: A synthwave track built entirely on free plugins (Surge XT + Cassette Drums) with a Tron-glow vector visual.

showcase.title: Spectrum
showcase.blurb: A live 3D FFT equaliser assembled from separate lane nodes - an AudioSpectrum node feeds per-band bar heights, a LanePalette node the colour gradient, through the new value-lane transport. Each bar is one frequency of the sound Vivid is making.

showcase.title: Blob
showcase.blurb: A raymarched SDF metaball that swells, melds and glows to the kick - the bass drives its size, its smooth-union blend and its emission through the audio→visual bridge, fast-attack then glide.

showcase.title: Crystal
showcase.blurb: Three different forms - a spiky crystal, a smooth churning orb, a torus ring - that a bar-locked Clock cuts between every 4 bars via a Switch3D node. Each churns to the bass and erupts note-spikes to the arp.

showcase.title: Storm
showcase.blurb: A GPU curl-noise particle storm - transients burst new embers into the field, the kick churns the turbulence and swells the particles.
